learning_outcomes.text: To get acquainted with the basic principles of Wave and Optics.
To know the basic principles of Electromagnetism as well as their application in Optics and in the Geometric Optics approximation.
To know the basic operation principles of optical systems.
To solve problems related to light propagation through complex optical systems.
To become familiar with the phenomenon of optical anisotropy.
To know the basic principles that govern the wave propagation as well as the phenomena of interference and diffraction.
To know the description of the polarization the transverse waves.
To solve problems related to light propagation through polarized optical systems.
To understand the basic principles of wave propagation.
To be able to analytically describe transverse waves, that propagate at an arbitrary direction, in any medium, for any polarization.
To be able to identify wave phenomena in nature.
To be able to describe both qualitatively and quantitatively the behavior of an optical system.
To be able to select and effectively use optical metrology techniques.
To use international literature to be informed about matters of Optics and Photonics.

syllabus_topics: Sources and detectors of optical radiation
teaching_methods: Demonstration experiments of basic optical phenomena
Open and free educational material (lecture slides, solved and unsolved exercises, simulations and animations, video-recorded lectures)
Optional student projects monitored through eClass platform
assessment_rules: Student performance is evaluated through final written exams. Alternatively, students may participate in optional projects, where the evaluation is split between a 20% presentation and 80% final written exams. The participation in projects is optional, and the project grade is auxiliary to the mentioned percentages. The evaluation criteria are accessible on the class webpage.
